text:
emma (Support): FYI customer acme-prod says their service account is getting 403s on project console actions and on API calls after we moved the project to a different org. Repro steps below, they provided logs. @raj can you triage?

maria (Customer Success): Which region/org-id? Also did they use SCIM to provision the service account earlier?

emma (Support): Region us-west1, old org id = org-1234, new org id = org-9876. The SA was originally provisioned via SCIM mapping (okta) and then invited to the project. They then triggered an org transfer via our console.

emma (Support): Repro (from customer):
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SA_TOKEN" "https://console.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proj-ACME/actions" -X POST -d '{"action":"deploy"}'
2) Response: HTTP/1.1 403
   Body: {"error":"permission_denied","message":"insufficient_scope","code":403}

emma (Support): They also see console UI with buttons greyed out: "You don't have permission to perform this action" when logged in as that SA (they use the SA session via API key proxy).

raj (SRE): Thanks. Quick guess: bindings weren't migrated to the new org's project row; sounds like role_binding entries still point to the old org_id or got orphaned during the transfer job. Do you have a DB snapshot or a role list for proj-ACME?

emma (Support): Customer shared this anonymized snippet: 
```
select * from role_binding where principal_id = 'sa:acme-service-1' and project_id = 'proj-ACME';
-- returns 0 rows
```
They confirmed the SA used to have `project:admin` on that project before transfer.

oliver (Product): Could this be related to SCIM group rename during the transfer? If the SA was getting roles via group membership rather than direct binding, the group-to-principal mapping might have broken.

devops-bot: Incident created IN-2026-034: "project move -> orphaned role bindings" (assigned to eng-infra).

raj (SRE): If it's 0 rows that's the issue. Workaround: create a direct binding back to the SA for the project. Example API call for support to run on behalf of customer:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proj-ACME/role-bindings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer SUPPORT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"principal":"sa:acme-service-1","role":"project:editor","source":"manual-support-rebind"}'
```
That should immediately restore both console and API privileges. Did they accept that temporary approach?

emma (Support): Yes, we ran the manual bind for them just now and they confirmed access restored. They still want to know why it happened and for a permanent fix.

raj (SRE): I'll open a postmortem and a bug. Initial hypothesis: transfer job does a shallow update of project.org_id but doesn't atomically update/repair dependent role_binding rows when principals are external (SCIM-provisioned) and group-mapped. Edge case when a principal is represented both as direct SA binding and group membership may cause double-delete.

oliver (Product): Can you check if the transfer flow emits events for a role-binding reparent step? If not we should add a reconciliation stage. Also check for any errors in the transfer job logs around the transfer timestamp.

raj (SRE): Will do. I need the transfer job id and approximate time window from the customer (they said transfer completed ~2026-03-06 16:12 UTC). Can you push the logs and any failed reconciliation entries?

emma (Support): Pushed customer-provided transfer job id: tr-2026-1138. I also attached the customer's `x-request-id` from the 403: `req-5a9c2f7b`.

raj (SRE): OK grabbing logs. Early plan: patch the transfer job to (1) lock project row during reparent, (2) run an explicit rebind/resync for role_binding entries (and group membership expansion), (3) emit an audit event. Short-term: a DB migration script to scan recent transfers and rebind missing principals. Medium-term: fix transfer job.

maria (Customer Success): Customer accepted the manual bind and is happy for now but wants ETA on an official fix and a runbook so they can handle this if it recurs.

raj (SRE): ETA: hotfix migration script within 72 hours to hunt and fix obvious orphaned bindings from recent transfers (risk: low, will run in read-only dry-run first). Full transfer-job patch estimate 2 weeks + QA. I'll create a follow-up ticket and include a runbook for support to rebind safely.

emma (Support): Great, I'll let the customer know and coordinate the follow-up. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Ticket INFRA-742 opened for the transfer reparent bug (link: https://issues.redwood.ai/INFRA-742)

raj (SRE): Filing postmortem after migration run. If anyone has related cases (same symptom after transfers), drop them here so we can aggregate.

emma (Support): I'll search backlog and add any hits. Closing this thread for now.
